tweets.text:
Investors have rarely been this bullish on tech.

Long speculative positioning in Nasdaq futures is up to nearly 50% of open interest, its highest since 2017.

This covers hedge funds, CTAs, and other institutional investors trading Nasdaq futures.

In other words, the net long Nasdaq futures position of these investors equals ~50% of all currently open Nasdaq futures contracts.

This marks a sharp reversal from a net short position as a % of open interest just a few weeks ago.

By comparison, Nasdaq net long positioning was below 25% of open interest for most of 2021-2025.

Meanwhile, net short positioning in Russell 2000 futures is down to -30% of open interest, its most bearish level since late 2025.

Investors are becoming extremely bullish on tech.

tweets.text:
The US corporate high-yield bond market is under serious pressure.

The effective yield on US high-yield corporate bonds is up to 8.03%, its highest since April 2025.

This figure has surged +104 basis points over the last 5 weeks, marking its largest 5-week increase in 17 months.

As a result, high-yield corporate bond spreads are up to 3.02%, their highest since early-April. 

This represents the extra yield investors demand, on average, to hold corporate junk bonds over Treasuries.

Meanwhile, average spreads for CCC-rated corporate bonds, the lowest-quality tier, have soared +400 basis points since January, to 968 basis points, their highest since November 2023.

US credit market stress is intensifying.

The trend is clear. Product-market fit remains paramount. But on its own, it won't be enough. Protocols need to show supply discipline and value accrual alongside it.

Short vibes. Long fundamentals.
